newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a declaration to be issued at the close of their summit today in Subic, the 18 APEC leaders will call for the early liberalisation of more industries and spell out details to fast-track translation of the forum's free trade blue print into action. (THE MANILA TIMES)
- Braving heavy rains, roadblocks and checkpoints, thousands of protestors from three groups set out for Olongapo on Sunday to press their case against free trade (THE MANILA TIMES)

- Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Sunday avoided discussions with U.S. President Bill Clinton on the human rights situation in China during bilateral talks, which focused on China's application to the World Trade Organisation. (TODAY)
- About 12,000 Filipino women cheered loudly as U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton urged them to support equality for women around the world. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- At least 67 people died when an Ethiopian Airlines plane crashed off the Comoro Islands on Saturday after it ran out of fuel during a hijacking attempt. (MALAYA)
- The Philippine and U.S. governments are unlikely to forge an agreement to settle a dispute on the new U.S. rules of origin on garments by the end of the APEC meet. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto announced that Japan would extend a 124.3 billion yen ($1.3 billion) loan package to the Philippines in talks with President Fidel Ramos on Sunday, a senior Japanese foreign ministry official said. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The Monetary Board of the Philippine Central Bank has approved the $150 million to $200 million 10-year bond issue of the National Power Corp, but advised the state-owned power firm to defer the flotation to next year to take advantage of the sovereign credit upgrade expected in 1997. (THE MANILA TIMES)
